The company's operations expose it to a variety of financial risks, which the company actively monitors, manages and acts upon, to mitigate such risks and their adverse effects.

								Credit Risk

								The company's policy is to ensure appropriate viability and credit checks on existing and potential customers are carried out regularly, and prior to any significant orders. Additionally, the company proactively ensures payment terms are agreed and followed.

								Exchange Rate Risk

								The company is exposed to limited currency risk with respect to inventory purchases denominated in currencies other than Pound Sterling. The company's policy is to purchase foreign currency to settle supplier payments using the spot rate.

								Interest Rate Cash Flow Risk

								There are no significant interest-bearing assets, the income and operating cash flows are independent of changes in Market Interest Rates.

								Liquidity Risk

								The company is in a cash-generative position and has sufficient funds for its operations and future planned growth.

								Conflict Risk

								The company is aware of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and has assessed its potential impact on the business. At the date of this report, the company does not consider there to be any material impact arising from the conflict. The company will continue to actively monitor developments and assess any material implications for the business as the situation continues.

The company operates a defined benefit pension scheme which was closed to new entrants on 1 April 2005 and ceased future accrual to existing members on 31 December 2006. The old scheme has been replaced with a new defined contribution scheme. 

The new scheme is a group personal pension plan which was implemented from January 2007. It is a money purchase scheme managed by Friends Life Group. Employees are required to contribute a minimum of 3% and the company will contribute 6% of an employee's gross pay. Contributions to the defined contribution scheme are recognised in the income statement in the year in which they become payable. 

For the defined benefit obligation scheme, the amounts charged to operating profit are the current service costs and gains and losses on settlements and curtailments. They are included as part of staff costs.

Past service costs are recognised immediately in the income statement if the benefits have vested. If the benefits have not vested immediately, the costs are recognised over the year until vesting occurs. The interest cost and the expected return on assets are shown as an amount net of other finance costs adjacent to interest. Actuarial gains and losses are recognised immediately in the Income Statement. 

The defined benefit obligation scheme is funded, with the assets of the scheme held separately from those of the company, in separate trustee administered funds. Pension scheme assets are measured at fair value and liabilities are measured on an actuarial basis using the projected credit until method and discounted at a rate equivalent to the current rate of return on a high-quality corporate bond of equivalent currency and term of the scheme liabilities. The actuarial valuations are obtained at least triennially and are updated at each balance sheet date. The resulting defined benefit or liability, net of the related deferred tax, is presented separately after other net assets In the Balance Sheet. 

The assumption for the revaluation rate used to increase deferred pensions prior to retirement is in line with Consumer Prices Index (CPI) inflation as the minimum statutory increases that will apply to the majority of pensions in deferment (those pensions in excess of Guaranteed Minimum Pensions). This was changed during the year ended 31 March 2011 and the previous policy which applied was where the deferred pension revaluation assumption was based on Retail Price Index (RPI) inflation. This change was in line with the government announcement on 08 July 2010, stating its intention to move from using RPI to using CPI inflation for statutory minimum increases in deferred pensions, and also in line with legal advice received from the Plan's lawyers regarding the operation of the Plan Rules in this regard.

The company also operates a defined benefit pension scheme. Under the scheme rules the company has an unconditional right to refund therefore the scheme surplus has been recognised in line with IFRIC 14.

A full actuarial valuation was carried out as at 31 March 2026. The pension scheme is closed to all its members for future accruals. In this financial year the company has contributed £663,510 plus the expenses of the scheme as part of the funding negotiations and expects to make further contributions of £330,582 for the year starting 1 April 2026. The scheme was closed to future accrual in December 2006.

The risks of the scheme are as follows: 

(a) Asset volatility

The scheme liabilities are calculated using a discount rate set with reference to corporate bond yields; if

scheme assets underperform this yield, this will create a deficit. The scheme holds a significant proportion
